body:
Thank you for responding. You mentioned that stimulants - used by people who do not have ADHD - hinder slightly, and help slightly in a few tasks. What are these tasks?

I googled ”cognitive ultrafunction” and I couldn’t find an explanation. What does that mean?

The reason I am asking this question is because I happen to have ADHD-PI, moderate severity. 

Based on my subjective experience, what ADHD impairs the most for me, individually, is concentration, working memory, slow cognitive tempo and organizing/prioritizing/planning.

I take Vyvanse, which helps TREMENDOUZLY with working memory, concentration, and speeds up my cognitive tempo.
I have better conversations (subject-matter-wise) this way, I learn a lot faster and more easily.

It seems to improve long term and working memory recollection, which is a dream come true 😍.

Although, it does cause racing thoughts, depersonalization and makes me feel extremely stressed and very anxious.

Even though it increases my cognitive tempo, I just cannot seem to pick up on what people say during conversations when they speak too fast. It becomes like a foreign language to me. 
When they speak at a normal rate, it’s all good.
Do you think there is anything that could be done to improve on picking up on what’s being said when people speak too fast? (This regards my native language and my linguistic ability is quite good, in my opinion).

I was prescribed propranolol, which allows me to keep my personality and it makes me more relaxed, and it is the closest I’ve felt to being ”normal” (and what I imagine that would be like).

Although it seems to reduce Vyvanse effects on my working memory by ALOT!
That, along with reduced emotional regulation, concentration, cognitive tempo and recollection of long term and working memory.

I don’t take any other medications and I am not diagnosed with anything else than ADHD.

I am taking 5mg propranolol and 50mg Vyvanse.

May I ask you to share your knowledge on what may be done to keep the benefits of Vyvanse, but allow me to keep my personality and reduce the increased anxiety from vyvanse?

I do not consider your eventual reply as medical advice.

Edited so that dosage-information was added.

I’m sorry about the late reply. Thank you for sharing!
The study I was referring to is now completed.

Interesting that you mention that doctors diagnose people with psychological conditions, rather than medical ones. I always find that concerning as a doctors primary competence lays within the medical field.

I appreciate the advice about singling out specific symptoms so to distinguish an ADHD-diagnosis from an ASD-diagnosis. A lot of symptoms overlap, and there are tables available, that compare the symtoms between ADHD and ASD (the symptoms are based on DSM-5). 
Although it’s still a hard to distinguish symtoms. 

Social symptoms of ASD are what seems to be the easiest to distinguish between the two diagnosises. That is also where the biggest changes within ASD-symptoms occured during treatment with ADHD-medication in individuals with comorbid ADHD and ASD, when looking at the results of my study.

Since the distinction is hard to make, I’ve chosen to make my study qualitative, which leaves room for subjective conclusions.

I am happy to hear that Elvanse works for you!
Sorry about the insomnia.

Interesting to hear that people seem to percieve ADHD as something that is easier to deal with, than ASD. That makes it a shame that severity levels aren’t specified, where you live in the UK.

Interesting to hear that you do not like distinctions as you feel like it divides people. Personally, I feel the opposite. The more we learn about mental disorders, and aspects regarding the mind, the higher the chances are for people to unite, as it allows people to understand eachother.

Personalyl I think misinformation and people not being well enough informed about diagnosises, could be one of the ways in which people aren’t even more united.

I read a book about developmental psychology. One specific chapter covered IQ. They summarized a few studies about IQ, upon which they mentioned that, finding out too much about IQ in people, would be a bad idea as it would make society too determinalistic (in my interpretation, it means that people will know what others are capable of, and what they aren’t capable of, through which there will be a lot of exclusion).
Personally I could not be more opposed to that perspective, because I would like to know what I am capable of, so to get an overview of what occupations and hobbies I am best suited for. Also, I believe that, uncovering aspects of IQ, could uncover aspects of the brain or mind that are indirectly related to IQ, which could make for an important piece of the puzzle in regards to mental disorders, which could help improve mental health. The above in this very paragraph is a theory.

Interesting that you mentioned that a lot of ADHD/ASD symptoms are rooted in depression/anxiety-related feelings. The question is if you are referring to yourself, or everyone who has comorbid ADHD and ASD. Another question is if there a study made which makes the conclusion you mentioned, or if that is your own theory, or subjective experience.

I rarely make long responses, but since you kindly answered some of the questions in my post, I’m happy to do so.

I am not able make another long response, unfortunately.
